text: The cubital fossa. The most needled triangle in your body. Let's dissect it.
First incision, along the front of the elbow.
In the superficial fascia: the cephalic vein laterally, the basilic vein medially, and the median cubital vein joining them. That's where blood is drawn.
Beside them run the lateral and medial cutaneous nerves of the forearm.
The roof is deep fascia, reinforced by the bicipital aponeurosis, which shields the artery underneath.
The boundaries. Above, a line between the two epicondyles. Laterally, brachioradialis. Medially, pronator teres. They meet at the apex.
The floor is brachialis, and supinator.
Contents, from lateral to medial: radial nerve, biceps tendon, brachial artery, median nerve.
Remember: Really Need Beer To Be At My Nicest.
At the apex, the brachial artery divides into the radial and ulnar arteries.
